records.change: Light called "beautiful" instead of "good"
records.note: A translation choice for Hebrew tov, which the ISV renders "good" elsewhere in the chapter; "beautiful" narrows the verdict on creation's goodness.

records.change: "living soul" becomes "living being"; "lungs" for "nostrils"
records.note: Translation choice for the Hebrew nephesh chayyah, which can mean soul or living creature. The Masoretic text is followed either way.

records.change: "as gods" becomes "like God"
records.note: The Hebrew elohim can be read as plural gods or as God; a translation choice on the Masoretic text.

records.change: Adds Cain's words "Let's go out to the wilderness"
records.note: The words are in the Samaritan Pentateuch, Septuagint and Syriac but not in the Masoretic text, which the KJV follows.

records.change: "Sons of God" becomes "divine beings"
records.note: An interpretive rendering of bene ha-elohim that settles the passage on the angelic reading; the Hebrew leaves the identity of the "sons of God" open.

records.change: "Sons of God" becomes "divine beings"
records.note: As in 6:2, a translation choice that commits to the angelic interpretation of bene ha-elohim, which the KJV's literal wording leaves open.

records.change: "Noah found grace" becomes "the LORD was pleased with Noah"
records.note: A translation choice for matsa chen; the Hebrew speaks of favour found by Noah, which the ISV recasts as God's approval of him, losing the note of grace given.

records.change: Omits "the rain from heaven was restrained"
records.note: The clause is in the Masoretic text; the ISV leaves it out of this verse and does not carry it into 8:3. The flood's ending is still described.

records.change: "My Lord" becomes "My lords"
records.note: The Masoretic text points the word as Adonai, the divine title addressed to one; the ISV reads the consonants as an ordinary plural addressed to the three visitors.

records.change: "My Lord" becomes "my lords"
records.note: As in 18:3, the Masoretic vowels give Adonai, the divine title; the ISV takes it as a plural courtesy address to the angels.

records.change: "it shall be seen" becomes "he will provide"
records.note: The Masoretic vowels read a passive "it shall be seen"; the ISV reads the verb as active, matching the name given to the place.

records.change: "The virgin" becomes "the young woman"
records.note: The Hebrew is almah, the word of Isaiah 7:14; the KJV renders it "virgin" here too, while the ISV's "young woman" bears on how that prophecy is read.

records.change: "God" becomes "the LORD"
records.note: The Hebrew has ha-Elohim, not the divine name YHWH; the ISV substitutes the covenant name, a translation choice.

records.change: Esau's dwelling "away from" fatness and dew, not with them
records.note: The Hebrew preposition min can mean "of" or "away from"; the KJV reads a blessing like Jacob's, the ISV a deprivation, which reverses the sense.

records.change: "The LORD shall add" becomes "May God give"
records.note: The Masoretic text has the divine name YHWH; the ISV renders it with the generic "God", a translation choice.

records.change: Omits "the God of their father"; Nahor's "god" lower-case
records.note: The phrase is in the Masoretic text but absent from the Septuagint, which the ISV appears to follow; the lower-case "god" also makes Nahor's deity a different one.

records.change: Omits "Joseph was a goodly person, and well favoured"
records.note: The clause is in the Masoretic text and is not carried into 39:7 in this text; it sets up the temptation that follows but carries no doctrine.

records.change: "Went out from the presence of Pharaoh" becomes "independent from Pharaoh's oversight"
records.note: A translation choice; the Hebrew says only that Joseph left Pharaoh's presence, and the ISV's reading adds a claim of independence not stated there.

records.change: "bowed himself upon the bed's head" becomes "collapsed on his bed"
records.note: A translation choice on the Masoretic text that drops the sense of worship; Hebrews 11:21, following the Septuagint, has him worshipping on his staff.

records.change: "digged down a wall" becomes "lamed cattle"
records.note: The Masoretic vowels give "hamstrung an ox"; the KJV read the consonants as "wall". A translation choice.

records.change: "until Shiloh come" becomes "until the One comes, who owns them both"
records.note: The ISV reads shiloh as shelloh, "whose it is", as the Septuagint and Targums do, rather than as a name. The messianic sense remains.

records.change: "From thence is the shepherd" becomes "in the name of the Shepherd"
records.note: The Masoretic text reads misham, "from there"; the ISV follows a repointing as mishem, "by the name", as in the Syriac. The titles Shepherd and Rock of Israel remain.

records.change: "The LORD" becomes "God"
records.note: The Masoretic text has the divine name YHWH here; the ISV renders it with the generic "God", a translation choice.

records.change: "The LORD said" becomes "God asked"
records.note: The Masoretic text has YHWH as the speaker; the ISV uses "God", though "I, the LORD" is kept at the end of the verse.

records.change: Statement "was I not known" made a question, reversing it
records.note: A translation choice: the Masoretic text has no question marker, and the ISV's question says the patriarchs knew the name LORD, the opposite of the KJV.

records.change: "kill" becomes "murder"
records.note: The Hebrew ratsach usually means unlawful killing; a translation choice on the Masoretic text that narrows the commandment's wording.

records.change: "her fruit depart" becomes "children are born prematurely"
records.note: A translation choice on the Hebrew "her children come out"; the KJV leaves it open to miscarriage, the ISV reads a live premature birth.

records.change: "Filled with the spirit of wisdom" becomes "endowed with talent"
records.note: A translation choice for ruach chokmah; the Hebrew presents the craftsmen's skill as a spirit God gives, which "talent" leaves out. Exodus 31:3 states the same gift.

records.change: Omits "as the LORD commanded Moses"
records.note: The refrain is in the Masoretic text and is not carried into 39:22 in this text; the same refrain recurs through the chapter.

records.change: Omits the priests bringing and sprinkling the blood on the altar
records.note: The clause is in the Masoretic text and the Septuagint and is not carried into 1:6 in this text; the blood rite at the heart of the burnt offering is lost here, though Leviticus 1:11 and 1:15 keep it.

records.change: Omits "and shall bear his iniquity"
records.note: The clause is in the Masoretic text; the guilt of an unknowing sinner is still stated, but his bearing of iniquity before atonement in 5:18 is dropped.

records.change: Atonement "for it" (the altar) becomes "for himself"
records.note: The Masoretic text has alav, referring to the altar, which 16:19 goes on to cleanse; the ISV makes the high priest the object, a translation choice.

records.change: Omits "I am the LORD"
records.note: The formula is in the Masoretic text and is not carried into 18:22; it grounds the command in God's name, as the chapter does elsewhere.

records.change: "I am the LORD your God" shortened to "I am the LORD"
records.note: The Masoretic text has YHWH Eloheichem; the ISV drops "your God", a small loss in the covenant formula.

records.change: Omits "I am the LORD your God"
records.note: The formula is in the Masoretic text and is not carried into 19:26 in this text; it recurs throughout the chapter.

records.change: Omits "I am the LORD your God"
records.note: The formula is in the Masoretic text and is not carried into 19:35 in this text; the command to love the stranger loses its stated ground in God's name.

records.change: Omits "their blood shall be upon them"
records.note: The clause is in the Masoretic text, and the ISV renders it in the neighbouring verses; here it is left out, though the death penalty is kept.

records.change: "I am the LORD your God" becomes "I am your God"
records.note: The Masoretic text has the divine name YHWH, which the ISV drops here, a translation choice.

records.change: "Holy unto the LORD" becomes "set apart to God"
records.note: The Masoretic text has the divine name YHWH; the ISV renders it with the generic "God".

records.change: Omits "under the hand of Ithamar the son of Aaron"
records.note: The clause is in the Masoretic text and is not carried into 7:9 in this text; Ithamar's oversight of the Merarites is still stated in Numbers 4:33.

records.change: This copy lacks Moses renaming Hoshea as Joshua
records.note: Not a translation difference: the clause is in the Hebrew and in the printed ISV but missing from this e-Sword copy of the ISV, and not carried into the next verse. Read it in the KJV here.

records.change: This copy lacks "the glory of the LORD appeared"
records.note: Not a translation difference: the clause is in the Hebrew and in the printed ISV but missing from this e-Sword copy of the ISV, and not carried into the next verse. It is the LORD's appearing that stops the stoning.

records.change: "it shall be our righteousness" becomes "credited as righteousness"
records.note: A translation choice: the Hebrew says it "will be righteousness for us"; the ISV's "credited" borrows the wording of Genesis 15:6 and reads imputation into the verse.

records.change: Adds "by fire" to "destroy thee suddenly"
records.note: The Masoretic text has only "destroy you quickly"; "by fire" has no basis in the Hebrew and is the translators' addition.

records.change: "the hornet" becomes "plagues"
records.note: A translation choice: the rare Hebrew tsir'ah is usually taken as "hornet" (so the Septuagint and Exodus 23:28 in most versions); the ISV reads it figuratively.

records.change: Omits "for the wickedness of these nations the LORD doth drive them out"
records.note: The clause is in the Masoretic text; the ISV leaves it out, perhaps as repeated, since verse 5 states it.

records.change: Omits "Not for thy righteousness, or for the uprightness of thine heart"
records.note: The clause is in the Masoretic text; the ISV's "On the contrary" replaces it, so the denial of Israel's uprightness of heart is lost, though verse 6 says they are not righteous.

records.change: "a damsel that is a virgin" becomes "a girl"; "lie with" becomes "rapes"
records.note: A translation choice: the Hebrew has betulah (virgin), which the ISV leaves out, and it reads the act as rape where the KJV says "lay hold on her, and lie with her".

records.change: Omits "for ever" after "tenth generation"
records.note: The Masoretic text has 'ad-'olam (for ever); the ISV keeps only "to the tenth generation", which may be read as a limit rather than a permanent exclusion (compare Nehemiah 13:1).

records.change: "whore" and "sodomite" become "cultic prostitutes"
records.note: The Hebrew qedeshah and qadesh are tied to shrine prostitution; a translation choice that narrows the prohibition to cult practice.

records.change: "upon thy seed for ever" becomes "as long as you live"
records.note: A translation choice: the Hebrew 'ad-'olam is "for ever"; the ISV limits the sign to the hearers' lifetime.

records.change: "children of Israel" becomes "children of God"
records.note: The ISV follows a Dead Sea Scroll (4QDeut-j) and the Septuagint ("angels of God") where the Masoretic text has "sons of Israel"; the reading ties the nations' boundaries to heavenly beings rather than to Israel.

records.change: "the lowest hell" becomes "the deepest part of Sheol"
records.note: A translation choice: the Hebrew is she'ol, which the ISV transliterates where the KJV has "hell".

records.change: "a fiery law" becomes "flaming fire"; the law is dropped
records.note: The Masoretic 'eshdat is obscure; the KJV reads it as "fire of law", the ISV as fire alone. A translation choice.

records.change: "the LORD shall cover him" becomes "the Most High protecting him"
records.note: The Masoretic text has "upon him" ('alayw), where the KJV supplies "the LORD"; the ISV follows an emendation to 'elyon (Most High). God is still the one who shelters Benjamin.

records.change: "my lord" becomes "Lord", addressing the commander as God
records.note: A translation choice: the Masoretic text points the word as adoni (my lord), a human title; the ISV's capital "Lord" treats the commander of the LORD's army as divine, a reading many interpreters also take.

records.change: Othniel, "Caleb's younger brother", becomes Caleb's nephew
records.note: A translation choice: the Hebrew "son of Kenaz, Caleb's younger brother" can refer to Othniel or to Kenaz; the ISV takes Kenaz as the brother, making Othniel a nephew.

records.change: "Oh my Lord" becomes "Sir"
records.note: The Masoretic text points the word here as Adonai, the title used of God, where verse 13 has adoni (my lord); the ISV reads both as a polite human address.

records.change: This copy lacks Gideon's call "Arise; for the LORD hath delivered"
records.note: Not a translation difference: the clause is in the Hebrew and in the printed ISV but missing from this e-Sword copy of the ISV, and not carried into the next verse. Verse 14 still says God has given Midian into his hand.

records.change: "an hollow place that was in the jaw" becomes "in Lehi"
records.note: A translation choice: the Hebrew lechi can be the jawbone or the place named after it; the ISV reads the place name, so the water no longer comes from the jaw.

records.change: "going to the house of the LORD" becomes "going home"
records.note: The Masoretic text has "the house of the LORD"; the ISV follows the Septuagint's "my house", which fits verse 29.

records.change: "an enemy in my habitation" becomes "Distress... in your household"; God unnamed
records.note: A translation choice for an obscure Hebrew line: the ISV reads the rival as distress in Eli's own house and has God speak in the first person.

records.change: Saul "30 years old" and reigned "42 years" supplied
records.note: The Masoretic numbers are defective; the ISV supplies 30 from some Septuagint manuscripts and 42 by emendation (compare Acts 13:21).

records.change: "covenant of the LORD" becomes "sacred covenant"
records.note: The Masoretic text reads "a covenant of the LORD"; the ISV renders it without the divine name, a translation choice. The covenant's sanction by the LORD is no longer stated.

records.change: Omits "establish it for ever" in David's prayer
records.note: The Masoretic text has "establish (it) for ever" (ad-olam); the ISV's paraphrase drops the "for ever". The everlasting Davidic promise is still stated in 2 Samuel 7:13, 16 and 29.

records.change: Omits "the LORD preserved David whithersoever he went"
records.note: The clause is in the Masoretic text and the Septuagint, and verse 7 does not carry it; this module's text lacks it. The same statement is still made in 2 Samuel 8:14.

records.change: King's words "he shall eat at my table" become narration
records.note: The Masoretic text has "at my table" as the king's speech; the Septuagint reads "at David's table", which the ISV follows as narration. The meaning is close, but the speaker changes.

records.change: Omits "the LORD struck the child" and "it was very sick"
records.note: The clause is in the Masoretic text and all ancient versions, and verse 16 does not carry it; this module's text lacks it. The child's illness as the LORD's judgment is otherwise implied only by verse 14.

records.change: Saws and harrows as forced labour; brickkiln omitted
records.note: A translation choice: "put them under saws" is read as labour with tools, not torture, and the ISV leaves out the qere reading "brickkiln".

records.change: Omits "the LORD had appointed to defeat the good counsel"
records.note: The sentence is in the Masoretic text and the ancient versions, and verse 15 does not carry it; this module's text lacks it. It is the narrator's statement of God's providence over Absalom's counsel.

records.change: Elhanan kills "Goliath", not "the brother of Goliath"
records.note: The Masoretic text lacks "the brother of", which the KJV supplies in italics from 1 Chronicles 20:5; the ISV's reading sits uneasily with 1 Samuel 17.

records.change: "hell" becomes "Sheol"
records.note: The Hebrew is sheol, which the KJV renders "hell" here and the ISV transliterates; a translation choice, not a textual difference. The poetic sense of mortal danger is the same.

records.change: Omits the region of Argob and its sixty walled cities
records.note: The clause is in the Masoretic text and the Septuagint, and verse 14 does not carry it; this module's text lacks it. The same towns are described in Deuteronomy 3:4 and 1 Chronicles 2:23.

records.change: "the LORD my God" becomes "the LORD"
records.note: The Masoretic text has "the LORD my God"; the ISV drops "my God", a translation choice. Solomon still says "the LORD my God" in verse 5.

records.change: Adds a second tribe "for the sake of Jerusalem"
records.note: The Masoretic text gives one tribe for both David's and Jerusalem's sake; the ISV's wording reads as two tribes. Verses 13 and 36 still speak of one tribe.

records.change: Omits "Thus saith the LORD God of Israel"
records.note: The prophetic formula is in the Masoretic text and the Septuagint, and verse 6 does not carry it; this module's text lacks it. Without it the words that follow are not marked as the LORD's.

records.change: "sodomites" becomes "male shrine prostitutes"
records.note: The Hebrew qadesh means a man consecrated to a shrine; a translation choice that ties the sin to cult practice.

records.change: "sodomites" becomes "male cult prostitutes"
records.note: The Hebrew qadesh means a man consecrated to a shrine; a translation choice that ties the sin to cult practice.

records.change: Omits the first "Thus saith the LORD"
records.note: The Masoretic text has the formula twice; the ISV keeps only the second, so the first question is not marked as the LORD's. The LORD's authorship of the judgment is still stated in the verse.

records.change: "sodomites" becomes "male cult prostitutes"
records.note: The Hebrew qadesh means a man consecrated to a shrine; a translation choice that ties the sin to cult practice.

records.change: Omits "Thus saith the LORD" in the messengers' report
records.note: The formula is in the Masoretic text and the Septuagint; this module's text lacks it. The message is still given as the LORD's in verses 3-4 and 16.

records.change: "the LORD his God" becomes "the LORD"
records.note: The Masoretic text has "the LORD his God"; the ISV drops "his God", a translation choice. The parallel in 2 Chronicles 28:1 also reads only "the LORD".

records.change: "the LORD your God" becomes "the LORD"
records.note: The Masoretic text has "the LORD your God"; the ISV drops "your God", a translation choice. The covenant relationship is still stated in verses 35-38.

records.change: "sodomites" becomes "cultic male prostitutes"; "grove" becomes "Asherah"
records.note: Translation choices for qadesh and asherah, naming the shrine practice and the goddess the KJV renders as a grove.

records.change: Omits the people anointing Jehoahaz king in Josiah's stead
records.note: The sentence is in the Masoretic text and the Septuagint, and verse 31 does not carry it; this module's text lacks it. The parallel is kept in 2 Chronicles 36:1.

records.change: Geshur and Aram take the towns, rather than being taken
records.note: The Hebrew makes Geshur and Aram the subject, as most modern versions read; the KJV makes them the object. A translation choice that reverses who conquered whom.

records.change: Pul and Tiglath-pileser made one king, "also known as"
records.note: A translation choice: the ISV reads the Hebrew "and" as explanatory, identifying Pul with Tiglath-pileser as historians do; the KJV reads two kings. The event itself is unchanged.

records.change: "like the host of God" becomes "a great, vast army"
records.note: A translation choice: the ISV takes "host of God" as a Hebrew superlative idiom, so the mention of God drops out. The size of David's army is still stated.

records.change: "the LORD blessed" becomes "God blessed"
records.note: The Masoretic text has the divine name (YHWH) here; the ISV renders it "God". The same blessing is told with "the LORD" in 2 Samuel 6:11.

records.change: second "ark of God" becomes "ark of the LORD"
records.note: The Masoretic text has "ark of God" both times; the ISV varies the second to "the LORD". The referent is the same.

records.change: Omits "Thus the LORD preserved David whithersoever he went"
records.note: The clause is in the Masoretic text; the ISV leaves it out here though it keeps the same line at 18:13. The LORD's preserving David is still stated there.

records.change: people dwelling in Jerusalem for ever becomes God residing in Israel
records.note: The Hebrew "and he dwells in Jerusalem for ever" has an unstated subject; the KJV makes it the people, the ISV makes it God and says "Israel" for Jerusalem.

records.change: "that he had by the spirit" becomes "had in mind"
records.note: The Hebrew "by the spirit with him" may mean inspiration or David's own mind; the ISV chooses the latter. The divine origin of the plan is still stated in 28:19.

records.change: keeping "this for ever" in the people's thoughts becomes God's purposes
records.note: A translation choice: the ISV makes the thoughts God's rather than the people's devotion, and drops "for ever". The prayer for their hearts to be directed to God remains.

records.change: Omits Solomon made king a second time, anointed, and Zadok priest
records.note: The clause is in the Masoretic text and is not carried in 29:23; the ISV text here ends after the feast. Solomon's reign is still stated in 29:23.

records.change: Omits Solomon's burial "in the city of David his father"
records.note: The clause is in the Masoretic text; the ISV shortens the verse. The burial is still recorded in 1 Kings 11:43.

records.change: "the Spirit of God" becomes "the Spirit of the LORD"
records.note: The Masoretic text has "Spirit of God" (Elohim); the ISV substitutes the divine name. The referent is the same.

records.change: "the LORD God of his father" becomes "the God of his ancestors"
records.note: The Masoretic text reads "the God of his father" here, without the divine name the KJV has; the ISV follows it. The same God is meant.

records.change: Ahaziah "22 years old", not forty-two; "granddaughter" of Omri
records.note: The Masoretic text has 42; the ISV follows some Septuagint manuscripts, the Syriac and 2 Kings 8:26, which have 22.

records.change: Omits "made him king", the anointing and "God save the king"
records.note: The clauses are in the Masoretic text and are not carried in 23:12; the ISV verse ends after the Testimony. The coronation is still told in 2 Kings 11:12.

records.change: "Moses the servant of God" becomes "servant of the LORD"
records.note: The Masoretic text has "servant of God" (Elohim); the ISV substitutes the divine name. Moses is called both elsewhere.

records.change: Omits his burial; "sons of Jehoiada" becomes "son"
records.note: The singular "son" follows the Septuagint and Vulgate where the Masoretic text has "sons"; the burial outside the royal tombs is in the Masoretic text but left out.

records.change: Omits "for ever" from God's promise to put his name there
records.note: The Masoretic text has "for ever" (le'olam); the ISV leaves it out, losing the permanence of the promise. It is still stated in 2 Kings 21:7.

records.change: Omits Cyrus taking the vessels out of the temple of Babylon
records.note: The clause is in the Aramaic text; the ISV compresses the verse. The vessels' return is still stated in Ezra 1:7-8.

records.change: "the sons of God" becomes "divine beings"
records.note: A translation choice: the Hebrew "bene ha-elohim" is rendered as a class of beings, dropping the filial wording. The heavenly council is still meant.

records.change: "The fire of God is fallen from heaven" becomes "A lightning storm"
records.note: A translation choice: "fire of God" is taken as an idiom for lightning, so the naming of God as its source drops out.

records.change: "the sons of God" becomes "divine beings"
records.note: A translation choice: the Hebrew "bene ha-elohim" is rendered as a class of beings, dropping the filial wording. The heavenly council is still meant.

records.change: "I have sinned" becomes "So what if I sin?"; burden to God
records.note: The first is a translation choice; "burden yourself" follows a reading noted by the scribes (tiqqun) instead of the Masoretic "to myself".

records.change: "deeper than hell" becomes "deeper than Sheol"
records.note: The Hebrew is "Sheol", which the KJV renders "hell" and the ISV transliterates. The contrast of height and depth remains.

records.change: "the firstborn of death" becomes "a deadly disease"
records.note: A translation choice: the ISV interprets the Hebrew idiom "firstborn of death" as a fatal illness rather than keeping the figure.

records.change: "my redeemer" becomes "my Vindicator"; "the Last One" stands
records.note: The Hebrew go'el covers redeemer and avenger; a translation choice that weakens the traditional messianic reading, though a living champion is still meant.

records.change: "Hell" and "destruction" become "Sheol" and "Abaddon"
records.note: The Hebrew words are "Sheol" and "Abaddon"; the ISV transliterates them where the KJV translates. God's sight of the realm of the dead is still stated.

records.change: "By his spirit" becomes "with his wind"
records.note: The Hebrew "ruach" can mean spirit or wind; the ISV chooses wind, losing a reading of the Spirit's part in creation.

records.change: "For God shall cast upon him" becomes "It will toss him"
records.note: The Hebrew has no stated subject; the KJV supplies "God" and the ISV takes the east wind of 27:21. God's judgment of the wicked is still the theme.

records.change: "this hast thou chosen rather than affliction" becomes tried beyond affliction
records.note: A difficult Hebrew line; the ISV's "tried" reads a different verb or an emendation, changing the warning's sense.

records.change: "all the sons of God" becomes "all the divine beings"
records.note: A translation choice: the Hebrew "bene elohim" is rendered as a class of beings, dropping the filial wording.

records.change: "Thou art my Son" becomes "son"; "begotten" becomes "become your father"
records.note: A translation choice on the Masoretic text: the lower-case "son" and "become your father" read the decree of the king rather than of the Messiah. The verse is applied to Christ in Acts 13:33 and Hebrews 1:5.

records.change: "Kiss the Son" becomes "Kiss the son"
records.note: The Hebrew "bar" is kept, but the lower case treats the son as the king rather than the Messiah. The messianic reading is still open from 2:7.

records.change: "lower than the angels" becomes "less than divine"
records.note: The Hebrew elohim can mean God or angels; the KJV follows the Septuagint's "angels", as Hebrews 2:7 quotes it.

records.change: "turned into hell" becomes "turn back to where the dead are"
records.note: The Hebrew is "Sheol", which the ISV renders as the place of the dead; the KJV's "hell" carries the sense of punishment.

records.change: "my Lord" becomes "my master"; "O my soul" dropped
records.note: "Adonai" is rendered with a common noun; "I told" follows the Septuagint and Syriac where the Masoretic text has "you (fem.) said", which the KJV fills with "O my soul".

records.change: "hell" becomes "Sheol"; "thine Holy One" becomes "your holy one"
records.note: The Hebrew is "Sheol" and "hasid"; the lower-case "holy one" reads the psalmist rather than the Messiah. Acts 2:27 and 13:35 apply the verse to Christ's resurrection.

records.change: "sorrows of hell" becomes "cords of Sheol"
records.note: The Hebrew is "Sheol", which the ISV transliterates. The psalmist's peril of death is unchanged.

records.change: "the word of the LORD" becomes "the word of God"
records.note: The Masoretic text has the divine name (YHWH) here; the ISV renders it "God". The same God is meant.

records.change: Voice heard everywhere becomes "their voice is not heard"
records.note: A translation choice on the Masoretic text: the ISV says creation speaks without words, the KJV that its voice reaches every language.

records.change: "thy Lord; and worship thou him" becomes "your lord, bow in respect"
records.note: A translation choice: "adon" in lower case and "bow" for the same Hebrew verb read the king as human. Hebrews 1:8-9 applies this psalm to Christ.

records.change: "go down quick into hell" becomes "plunged alive into the afterlife"
records.note: The Hebrew is "Sheol", which the ISV renders "the afterlife"; the KJV's "hell" carries the sense of punishment.

records.change: "the company of those that published it" becomes "the women"
records.note: The Hebrew participle is feminine; a translation choice that the KJV does not reflect.

records.change: "O LORD God of hosts" becomes "God of hosts"
records.note: The Masoretic text has the divine name (YHWH Elohim Tseba'ot), which the ISV leaves out; the verse is also paraphrased. The same God is addressed.

records.change: "O LORD" becomes "God"
records.note: The Masoretic text has the divine name YHWH here; the ISV renders it with the general word "God". The same God is meant.

records.change: "the lowest hell" becomes "the depths of Sheol"
records.note: Translation choice: the Hebrew is sheol, the realm of the dead, which the ISV transliterates where the KJV renders it "hell".

records.change: "Moses the man of God" becomes "the godly man"
records.note: Translation choice: the Hebrew 'ish ha'elohim is the usual title of a prophet; the ISV makes it a description of Moses' character.

records.change: "keep his anger for ever" becomes "remain distant"
records.note: Translation choice for the Hebrew yittor, "keep (anger)"; the ISV loses the reference to God's anger, which the parallel line still implies.

records.change: "trees of the LORD" becomes "loftiest trees"
records.note: Translation choice: the ISV reads the divine name as a superlative ("mighty trees"), where the KJV keeps the LORD as their owner and planter.

records.change: "they rebelled not" becomes "Did they not rebel?"
records.note: The Masoretic text has "not"; the Septuagint omits it. The ISV keeps the negative but makes a question, reversing the sense.

records.change: "provoked his spirit" becomes "rebelled against him"
records.note: Translation choice: the Hebrew "his spirit" can be God's Spirit (as Isaiah 63:10) or Moses'; the ISV drops the word spirit.

records.change: "pains of hell" becomes "anguish of Sheol"
records.note: Translation choice: the Hebrew is sheol, the realm of the dead, which the ISV transliterates where the KJV renders it "hell".

records.change: "word above all thy name" becomes word kept "consistent with your name"
records.note: Translation choice on a difficult Hebrew line: the KJV exalts God's word above his name; the ISV has God act to fulfil his word as his name requires.

records.change: "make my bed in hell" becomes "lay down with the dead"
records.note: Translation choice: the Hebrew is sheol, the realm of the dead. God's presence everywhere is still stated.

records.change: Adds "God is faithful about everything he says"; later verses shift
records.note: The Masoretic text lacks the nun line of this acrostic; the ISV supplies it from a Dead Sea Scroll (11QPs-a) and the Septuagint, so KJV verses 14-21 are its 15-22.

records.change: Omits the closing "Praise ye the LORD"
records.note: The Masoretic text ends the psalm and the Psalter with Hallelujah; the ISV's text of this verse has no closing word of praise.

records.change: "take hold on hell" becomes "lead to Sheol"
records.note: Translation choice: the Hebrew is sheol, the realm of the dead, which the ISV transliterates where the KJV renders it "hell".

records.change: "the way to hell" becomes "leads to Sheol"
records.note: Translation choice: the Hebrew is sheol, the realm of the dead, which the ISV transliterates where the KJV renders it "hell".

records.change: "The LORD possessed me" becomes "The LORD made me"
records.note: Translation choice: the Hebrew qanah can mean "acquire, possess" or "create". Wisdom here is often read of Christ, and "made" was the Arian reading of the Septuagint's ektise.

records.change: "depths of hell" becomes "depths of Sheol"
records.note: Translation choice: the Hebrew is sheol, the realm of the dead, which the ISV transliterates where the KJV renders it "hell".

records.change: "Hell and destruction" becomes "Sheol and Abaddon"
records.note: Translation choice: the ISV transliterates sheol and 'abaddon where the KJV translates them; the Hebrew is the same.

records.change: "hell beneath" becomes "Sheol below"
records.note: Translation choice: the Hebrew is sheol, the realm of the dead, which the ISV transliterates where the KJV renders it "hell".

records.change: "must shew himself friendly" becomes "can still be ruined"
records.note: The Hebrew verb can come from "be friendly" or "be broken"; a translation choice on the Masoretic text.

records.change: "deliver his soul from hell" becomes "from Sheol"
records.note: Translation choice: the Hebrew is sheol, the realm of the dead, which the ISV transliterates where the KJV renders it "hell".

records.change: "The great God that formed all things" becomes "An archer"
records.note: The Hebrew is obscure: rab can mean "great one" or "archer" and meholel "forming" or "wounding". The KJV reads a statement about God; the ISV a proverb about hiring fools.

records.change: "Hell and destruction" becomes "Sheol and Abaddon"
records.note: Translation choice: the ISV transliterates sheol and 'abaddon where the KJV translates them.

records.change: "the people perish" becomes "people abandon restraint"
records.note: The Hebrew para' means to let loose; a translation choice, and "vision" is made prophetic revelation.

records.change: "become his son" becomes "become ungrateful"
records.note: The Hebrew manon occurs only here and its meaning is uncertain; the KJV reads "son" (heir), the ISV a guess from context.

records.change: Names Agur, Jakeh, Ithiel, Ucal read as words
records.note: Translation choice or revocalisation: the ISV reads the names as "collector", "God with me" and "prevailed", so the proper names of the Masoretic text disappear.

records.change: "set the world in their heart" becomes "placed eternity within them"
records.note: The Hebrew 'olam can mean world or eternity; a translation choice.

records.change: "power over the spirit" becomes "control over the wind"
records.note: Translation choice: the Hebrew ruach means spirit, breath or wind. The KJV speaks of retaining the life-spirit at death; the ISV makes it a comparison with the wind.

records.change: Omits "mountain of the LORD" and "out of Zion...the law"
records.note: The Masoretic text and the parallel Micah 4:2 have both; the ISV's text leaves them out, so the law going out from Zion and Jerusalem is lost here.

records.change: "hell hath enlarged herself" becomes "Sheol's appetite has grown"
records.note: Translation choice: the Hebrew is sheol, the realm of the dead, which the ISV transliterates where the KJV renders it "hell".

records.change: "a virgin shall conceive" becomes "The young lady is conceiving"
records.note: Translation choice: the Hebrew 'almah means a young woman of marriageable age; the Septuagint has parthenos, virgin, and Matthew 1:23 quotes the verse of the virgin birth, which is still stated there.

records.change: "not increased the joy" becomes "increased its joy"
records.note: The written Hebrew (ketiv) has lo' "not"; the marginal reading (qere) has lo "to it". The KJV follows the ketiv, the ISV the qere, reversing the clause.

records.change: "Hell from beneath" becomes "The afterlife below"
records.note: Translation choice: the Hebrew is sheol, the realm of the dead, which the ISV transliterates where the KJV renders it "hell".

records.change: "O Lucifer, son of the morning" becomes "Day Star"
records.note: The Hebrew helel means "shining one"; the KJV follows the Vulgate's Lucifer, long read as a name of Satan. The ISV translates the word; the text is the same.

records.change: "brought down to hell" becomes "brought down to join the dead"
records.note: Translation choice: the Hebrew is sheol, the realm of the dead, which the ISV transliterates where the KJV renders it "hell".

records.change: Fish-pond makers become cloth workers and wage earners
records.note: The rare Hebrew words can be read as weavers and hired workers or as dams and ponds; a translation choice on the Masoretic text.

records.change: "with hell are we at agreement" becomes "with Sheol"
records.note: Translation choice: the Hebrew is sheol, the realm of the dead, which the ISV transliterates where the KJV renders it "hell".

records.change: "agreement with hell" becomes "agreement with Sheol"
records.note: Translation choice: the Hebrew is sheol, the realm of the dead, which the ISV transliterates where the KJV renders it "hell".

records.change: Omits "the LORD hath a sacrifice in Bozrah" clause
records.note: The Masoretic text has the clause about the sacrifice and slaughter in Bozrah and Edom; the ISV's text of this verse and the next leaves it out.

records.change: "the screech owl" becomes "Liliths"; "hyenas" for island beasts
records.note: The Hebrew lilith is a night creature or night demon; the ISV transliterates it, bringing in the name of a figure of Mesopotamian myth.

records.change: "inhabitants of the world" becomes "denizens of the grave"
records.note: The Masoretic text reads hedel, "cessation", which the ISV takes as the grave; the KJV's "world" reads heled, as many manuscripts do.

records.change: "God the LORD" becomes "God"
records.note: The Masoretic text has ha'el YHWH; the ISV leaves out the divine name. The same God is speaking.

records.change: "I the LORD have called thee" becomes "I've called you"
records.note: The Masoretic text has the divine name here; the ISV leaves it out. The speaker is the same, named in verse 5.

records.change: "thy Saviour" becomes "your Redeemer"
records.note: Translation choice: the Hebrew moshi'eka means "your Saviour"; the ISV uses another title. God is called Saviour again in verse 11.

records.change: "there is no God" becomes "There is no other Rock"
records.note: Translation choice: the Hebrew tsur is literally "rock", a title of God; the ISV keeps the literal title. The claim that there is no other God is still made.

records.change: "create evil" becomes "create disaster"
records.note: The Hebrew ra' covers moral evil and calamity; paired with "peace", many translations read calamity. A translation choice.

records.change: Omits "I the LORD have created it"; heavens made to shout
records.note: The Masoretic text ends with God claiming the work as his creation; the ISV's text leaves that clause out and recasts the rest.

records.change: "I have chosen thee" becomes "I have purified you"
records.note: The Masoretic text has bachar (chose); the Isaiah scroll from Qumran reads bachan (tested). The ISV's reading is closer to the scroll.

records.change: "the land of Sinim" becomes "the Aswan region"
records.note: Follows the Dead Sea Isaiah scroll's "Syene" (Aswan) instead of the Masoretic "Sinim".

records.change: Adds "light": "he will see light"
records.note: The ISV follows the Isaiah scrolls from Qumran and the Septuagint, which add "light"; the Masoretic text, which the KJV follows, lacks it. Often read of the Servant's resurrection.

records.change: "the king" becomes "Molech"; "hell" becomes "Sheol"
records.note: Translation choice: the Hebrew melek can be vocalised as the god Molech; the ISV also transliterates sheol where the KJV renders "hell".

records.change: Omits "the LORD saw it, and it displeased him"
records.note: The Masoretic text has this clause; the ISV's text leaves it out, so God's seeing and displeasure at the lack of justice is lost before verse 16.

records.change: "Spirit of the LORD" lifting a standard becomes "breath of the LORD"
records.note: The Hebrew allows either reading: the KJV has the enemy come like a flood and the Spirit resist him; the ISV has the LORD come like a stream driven by his breath.

records.change: "thy name is from everlasting" becomes "from long ago"
records.note: Translation choice: the Hebrew me'olam can mean "from eternity" or "from of old"; the ISV also joins it to "Redeemer" as God's name.

records.change: "remember iniquity for ever" becomes "for a season"
records.note: The Masoretic la'ad means "for ever"; the ISV's "for a season" is a translation choice that softens the plea's scope.

records.change: "that troop" and "that number" become "Fortune" and "Destiny"
records.note: The Hebrew Gad and Meni are taken as names of pagan gods rather than common nouns; a translation choice on the Masoretic text.

records.change: "the Lord GOD" becomes "the LORD"
records.note: The Hebrew has Adonai YHWH; the ISV renders only the divine name, a translation choice. Nothing of doctrine is lost.

records.change: Omits "we come unto thee; for thou art the LORD"
records.note: The clause is in the Masoretic text and is not carried in the neighbouring verses here; the people's confession of the LORD as their God is lost from this verse.

records.change: Omits "and will not repent"
records.note: The Masoretic text has "I will not relent" before "neither will I turn back"; the ISV keeps only the second, a translation choice that merges the two.

records.change: Omits "saith the LORD"
records.note: The formula ne'um YHWH is in the Masoretic text and is not in the next verse here; the speaker is still plain from context.

records.change: Omits "saith the LORD"
records.note: The formula ne'um YHWH is in the Masoretic text; the text here ends without it, though the LORD is plainly the speaker (15:19).

records.change: Omits "saith the LORD"
records.note: The formula ne'um YHWH is in the Masoretic text; the text here leaves it out, though the LORD is the speaker of the oracle.

records.change: "A woman shall compass a man" becomes "will protect a man"
records.note: A translation choice on an obscure Hebrew phrase that some older interpreters read of the virgin birth; the ISV's wording does not allow that reading.

records.change: "Ah Lord GOD" becomes "LORD"
records.note: The Hebrew has Adonai YHWH; the ISV gives one title, a translation choice.

records.change: "O Lord GOD" becomes "Lord"
records.note: The Hebrew has Adonai YHWH; the ISV drops the divine name and keeps "Lord", a translation choice.

records.change: Adds "we are going to continue offering sacrifices"
records.note: The Hebrew reads "when we burned incense" as part of the women's question; the ISV turns it into a vow to continue, a translation choice.

records.change: First "Lord GOD of hosts" becomes "LORD of the Heavenly Armies"
records.note: The Hebrew has Adonai YHWH Tseva'ot; the ISV drops "Lord" the first time only, a translation choice.

records.change: "O virgin daughter of Zion" becomes "fair one of Zion"
records.note: The Hebrew betulat bat-Tsiyyon is "virgin daughter of Zion"; the ISV renders it idiomatically, losing "virgin". No doctrine rests on it here.

records.change: "whither the spirit was to go" becomes "wherever they decided to go"
records.note: The Hebrew has ruach, the spirit that directs the living creatures; the ISV makes the creatures' own choice the guide, a translation choice.

records.change: "spirit of the living creature" becomes "the wheels were alive"
records.note: The Hebrew ruach hachayyah is read by the ISV as "life" rather than the creature's spirit, a translation choice; the spirit's direction of the wheels is lost.

records.change: "the spirit of the living creature" becomes "wheels were also alive"
records.note: As in 1:20, the ISV reads ruach hachayyah as "life", a translation choice.

records.change: "the Lord GOD" becomes "the LORD"
records.note: The Hebrew has Adonai YHWH; the ISV renders only the divine name, a translation choice.

records.change: Omits "I the LORD" and "I will be comforted"
records.note: Both are in the Masoretic text; the ISV's paraphrase leaves the divine name and the clause out.

records.change: "the spirit of the living creature" becomes "they were alive"
records.note: As in 1:20, the ISV reads ruach hachayyah as "life", a translation choice.

records.note: The Hebrew has Adonai YHWH; the ISV renders only the divine name, a translation choice.

records.change: "saith the Lord GOD" becomes "declares the LORD"
records.note: The Hebrew has Adonai YHWH; the ISV renders only the divine name, a translation choice.

records.change: "a vine in thy blood" becomes "a vine entwining a pomegranate"
records.note: The Masoretic text reads "in your blood"; the ISV follows a conjectural emendation of the Hebrew.

records.change: "saith the Lord GOD" becomes "declares the LORD"
records.note: The Hebrew has Adonai YHWH; the ISV renders only the divine name, a translation choice.

records.change: "saith the Lord GOD" becomes "declares the LORD"
records.note: The Hebrew has Adonai YHWH; the ISV renders only the divine name, a translation choice.

records.change: "saith the Lord GOD" becomes "declares the LORD"
records.note: The Hebrew has Adonai YHWH; the ISV renders only the divine name, a translation choice.

records.change: Omits "Thus saith the Lord GOD"
records.note: The formula is in the Masoretic text and is not in the neighbouring verses here; the LORD is still plainly the speaker.

records.change: "I am the Lord GOD" becomes "I am the LORD"
records.note: The Hebrew has Adonai YHWH; the ISV renders only the divine name, a translation choice.

records.change: "the Lord GOD" becomes "the LORD"
records.note: The Hebrew has Adonai YHWH; the ISV renders only the divine name, a translation choice.

records.change: "the Lord GOD" becomes "the LORD"
records.note: The Hebrew has Adonai YHWH; the ISV renders only the divine name, a translation choice.

records.change: "cast him down to hell" becomes "descending into Sheol"
records.note: The Hebrew is she'ol, which the ISV transliterates; a translation choice about the realm of the dead.

records.change: "went down into hell" becomes "went down into Sheol"
records.note: The Hebrew is she'ol, which the ISV transliterates; a translation choice.

records.change: Omits "saith the Lord GOD"
records.note: The formula ne'um Adonai YHWH is in the Masoretic text; the ISV leaves it out, though the LORD is the speaker of the oracle.

records.change: "out of the midst of hell" becomes "of Sheol"
records.note: The Hebrew is she'ol, which the ISV transliterates; a translation choice.

records.change: "gone down to hell" becomes "went straight to Sheol"
records.note: The Hebrew is she'ol, which the ISV transliterates; a translation choice.

records.change: Omits "saith the Lord GOD"
records.note: The oath formula ne'um Adonai YHWH is in the Masoretic text; the ISV leaves it out, though the LORD is plainly the speaker (34:7).

records.change: "the Lord GOD" becomes "the LORD"
records.note: The Hebrew has Adonai YHWH; the ISV renders only the divine name, a translation choice.

records.change: Omits "Thus saith the Lord GOD"
records.note: The formula is in the Masoretic text and not in the neighbouring verses here; the LORD is still plainly the speaker.

records.change: "the Lord GOD" becomes "the LORD"
records.note: The Hebrew has Adonai YHWH; the ISV renders only the divine name, a translation choice.

records.change: "a covenant of peace" becomes "a secure covenant"
records.note: The Hebrew is berit shalom, "covenant of peace"; the ISV renders shalom as security, a translation choice. The covenant is still everlasting.

records.change: Omits "to take away cattle and goods"
records.note: The phrase is in the Masoretic text; the ISV compresses it into "war booty".

records.change: Adds "Within a week"
records.note: Nothing in the Masoretic text gives a time for the handing over; the ISV adds it.

records.change: "like the Son of God" becomes "resembles a divine being"
records.note: The Aramaic bar-elahin can be read "a son of the gods"; the ISV takes it as a heavenly being, a translation choice. The KJV's reading is often taken as a pre-incarnate appearance of Christ.

records.change: "his father Nebuchadnezzar" becomes "his grandfather"
records.note: The Aramaic has "his father", which can mean ancestor or predecessor; the ISV interprets it historically.

records.change: "thy father" becomes "your grandfather"
records.note: The Aramaic has "your father", which can mean ancestor or predecessor; the ISV interprets it historically.

records.change: "the king my father" becomes "my grandfather the king"
records.note: The Aramaic has "my father", which can mean ancestor or predecessor; the ISV interprets it historically.

records.change: "Nebuchadnezzar thy father" becomes "your grandfather Nebuchadnezzar"
records.note: The Aramaic has "your father", which can mean ancestor or predecessor; the ISV interprets it historically.

records.change: "thou his son" becomes "his grandson"
records.note: The Aramaic has "his son", which can mean descendant or successor; the ISV interprets it historically.

records.change: Omits "the thrones were cast down" (set in place)
records.note: The clause is in the Masoretic Aramaic; the ISV leaves it out, losing the thrones of the judgment scene.

records.change: "O my God" becomes "Lord"
records.note: The Hebrew has Elohai, "my God"; the ISV's "Lord" is a translation choice. God is still the one addressed.

records.change: "the Messiah the Prince" becomes "the anointed commander"
records.note: The Hebrew mashiach nagid can be read as a title or generically; the ISV's lower-case rendering loses the KJV's reading of a named Messiah, though the seven and 62 weeks stay together.

records.change: "Messiah... not for himself" becomes "anointed one... no successor"
records.note: The Hebrew ve'ein lo is obscure; the ISV takes it as having no successor, and renders mashiach generically, so the KJV's reading of a Messiah cut off for others is lost.

records.change: "overspreading of abominations" becomes "destructive people" on "the pinnacle"
records.note: A translation choice on difficult Hebrew; "poured upon the desolate" also becomes "the desolator", shifting who suffers the decree.

records.change: "the God of his fathers" becomes "the gods of his ancestors"
records.note: The Hebrew elohei avotav can be singular or plural; the ISV reads it as pagan gods, a translation choice that changes whom the king rejects.

records.change: "utterly take them away" becomes "nor will I forgive them"
records.note: The Hebrew nasa can mean "take away" or "forgive"; the ISV chooses the second, a translation choice.

records.change: "like men" becomes "like Adam"
records.note: The Hebrew adam can be the name or "mankind"; a translation choice that points to a covenant with Adam.

records.change: "Who knoweth if he will return" becomes a confident "will he not"
records.note: The Hebrew mi yodea' expresses uncertainty; the ISV turns it into an expected answer, a translation choice.

records.change: "dig into hell" becomes "burrow into Sheol"
records.note: The Hebrew is she'ol, which the ISV transliterates; a translation choice.

records.change: "out of the belly of hell" becomes "from the depths of death"
records.note: The Hebrew is mibbeten she'ol; the ISV renders she'ol as death, a translation choice.

records.change: "enlargeth his desire as hell" becomes "like the afterlife"
records.note: The Hebrew is she'ol; the ISV renders it "the afterlife", a translation choice.

records.change: Omits the third "saith the LORD of hosts"
records.note: The Masoretic text has the formula three times; the ISV gives it twice. The speaker is unchanged.

records.change: "Grace, grace unto it" becomes "How beautiful! How beautiful!"
records.note: The Hebrew chen can mean grace or beauty; the ISV chooses the second, so the cry for God's favour on the temple is lost.

records.change: "unto the house of God" becomes "the people of Bethel"
records.note: The Hebrew beit-el can be read as "house of God" or the town Bethel; the ISV takes it as the town, a translation choice.

records.change: Omits "therefore came a great wrath from the LORD of hosts"
records.note: The clause is in the Masoretic text and is not in the next verse here; the LORD's wrath on their hardness is left unstated.

records.change: Omits "upon an ass"; only "a colt, the foal" remains
records.note: The Hebrew has both "on a donkey" and "on a colt, the foal of a donkey", as Matthew 21:5 quotes; the ISV gives only the second.

records.change: Omits mourning "as for his only son... his firstborn"
records.note: The clause is in the Masoretic text and is not in 12:11 here; the mourning for the pierced one, read in John 19:37 and Revelation 1:7 of Christ, is lost from this verse.

records.change: Omits the second "the king"
records.note: The critical text lacks the second ho basileus, which the Textus Receptus and Byzantine majority have; David's kingship is still stated earlier in the verse.

records.change: Omits "firstborn"; "a son" only
records.note: Sinaiticus and Vaticanus read "a son" where the Byzantine text and Textus Receptus read "her firstborn son"; Jesus is still called Mary's firstborn in Luke 2:7.

records.change: "Jesus" omitted; "he"
records.note: The critical text lacks ho Iesous, which the Textus Receptus has; the referent is plain from context.

records.change: Omits "bless them that curse you, do good..." and "despitefully use you"
records.note: The clauses are in the Byzantine majority and Textus Receptus but not in Sinaiticus or Vaticanus; similar wording remains in Luke 6:27-28.

records.change: Omits the doxology "For thine is the kingdom... Amen"
records.note: The doxology is in the Byzantine majority and Textus Receptus but absent from Sinaiticus, Vaticanus and other early witnesses; the ISV follows the latter.

records.change: Leper addresses Jesus as "Sir", not "Lord"
records.note: Both texts read kyrie; rendering it "Sir" is a translation choice that weakens the title given to Jesus by one who worshipped him.

records.change: Omits "Jesus saith unto them" and the reply "Lord"
records.note: Both are in the Textus Receptus and Byzantine text but not in Sinaiticus or Vaticanus; the disciples' address of Jesus as Lord is lost here.

records.change: "Jesus" omitted; "he"
records.note: The critical text lacks ho Iesous, which the Textus Receptus has; the referent is plain.

records.change: Omits "draweth nigh unto me with their mouth"
records.note: The clause is in the Byzantine text and Textus Receptus but not in Sinaiticus or Vaticanus, which match Isaiah 29:13 in the Septuagint more briefly.

records.change: "Jesus' feet" becomes "his feet"
records.note: The critical text reads autou where the Textus Receptus reads tou Iesou; the referent is plain.

records.change: "Jesus the Christ" becomes "the Messiah"
records.note: The critical text lacks Iesous, which the Textus Receptus has; his identity as the Christ is kept.

records.change: Omits "Jesus" and "first"
records.note: The critical text lacks ho Iesous and proton, both in the Textus Receptus; Elijah's coming first is still implied by verse 10.

records.note: The clause is in the Byzantine text and Textus Receptus but not in Sinaiticus and some others; the same teaching is in Matthew 5:32.

records.change: "Why callest thou me good... God" becomes "Why ask me about what is good"
records.note: The critical text follows Sinaiticus and Vaticanus; the Textus Receptus matches Mark 10:18 and Luke 18:19, where the question about Jesus being called good is kept.

records.change: Omits "to be baptized with the baptism that I am baptized with"
records.note: The clause is in the Byzantine text and Textus Receptus but not in Sinaiticus or Vaticanus; it stands in Mark 10:38.

records.change: "temple of God" becomes "the Temple"
records.note: The critical text lacks tou theou, which the Textus Receptus has; the Temple is still plainly God's house (verse 13).

records.change: "angels of God" becomes "angels"
records.note: Vaticanus and others lack theou, which the Textus Receptus and many witnesses have; the meaning is little changed.

records.change: Omits "even Christ" as the one Master
records.note: The critical text lacks ho Christos, which the Textus Receptus has; Christ is named as the one teacher in verse 10.
