records.note: The Textus Receptus and most manuscripts, with P46, read 'Christ'; Sinaiticus, Vaticanus and others read 'the Lord', which the ISV follows.

records.change: Omits "for the earth is the Lord's, and the fulness thereof"
records.note: The quotation is repeated from verse 26 in the Textus Receptus and later manuscripts but not in the early ones; it is still in verse 26.

records.change: Omits "Take, eat" and "broken"
records.note: The critical text, following the earliest manuscripts, reads "my body which is for you"; the Textus Receptus adds "Take, eat" and "broken". The body given for believers is still stated.

records.change: Omits "unworthily" and "Lord's" before "body"
records.note: Both words are in the Textus Receptus and later manuscripts but not in P46, original Sinaiticus, Alexandrinus or Vaticanus; 'unworthily' is still in verse 27.

records.change: "give my body to be burned" becomes "sacrifice myself"
records.note: The Textus Receptus reads 'be burned'; P46, Sinaiticus and others read 'that I may boast', and the ISV gives a general rendering of either.

records.change: "the Lord from heaven" becomes "came from heaven"
records.note: 'The Lord' is in the Textus Receptus and later manuscripts but not in P46, Sinaiticus, Vaticanus or others; the second man is still from heaven.

records.change: "the first day of the week" becomes "After the Sabbath ends"
records.note: A translation choice for the Greek 'on the first of the week'; the ISV's wording could be read as Saturday evening.

records.change: "the Lord Jesus Christ" becomes "the Lord"
records.note: 'Jesus Christ' is in the Textus Receptus and later manuscripts but not in P46, Sinaiticus, Alexandrinus or Vaticanus.

records.change: "our Lord Jesus Christ" becomes "the Lord Jesus"
records.note: 'Christ' is in the Textus Receptus and many manuscripts but not in original Sinaiticus, Vaticanus and others.

records.change: Omits the closing "Amen"
records.note: 'Amen' is in the Textus Receptus and many manuscripts but not in Vaticanus and others; the subscription after it is not part of the text.

records.change: Omits "and salvation" after the second "consolation"; clauses reordered
records.note: The Textus Receptus follows a different order of the clauses from the early manuscripts, repeating 'consolation and salvation'; the ISV follows the shorter order.

records.change: "the Lord Jesus" becomes "Jesus"
records.note: 'Lord' is in the Textus Receptus and later manuscripts but not in P46, Sinaiticus, Vaticanus and others.

records.change: "by Jesus Christ" becomes "through the Messiah"; "Jesus" dropped
records.note: The Textus Receptus reads "Jesus Christ"; the critical text, following early Alexandrian witnesses, has "Christ" alone. The reconciler is the same person in both.

records.change: Omits "that we would receive the gift"
records.note: The words "that we would receive" are in later manuscripts and the Textus Receptus but not in the early witnesses the critical text follows. The sense of the Macedonians' eagerness to give is unchanged.

records.change: "our Lord Jesus Christ" becomes "the Lord Jesus"
records.note: The critical text, following Sinaiticus, Vaticanus and others, lacks "our" and "Christ", which the Textus Receptus has. The title is shortened, not the doctrine.

records.change: Omits closing "Amen"
records.note: The final "Amen" is in the Textus Receptus and many later manuscripts but not in the early witnesses the critical text follows. The KJV's closing note on where the letter was written is a later subscription, not part of the verse.

records.change: "faith of the Son of God" becomes "faithfulness of the Son"
records.note: A translation choice: the ISV reads the Greek genitive as Christ's own faithfulness rather than the believer's faith in him. The Greek is the same in both texts; the change shifts the verse's emphasis on faith.

records.change: Omits "in Christ" from the covenant confirmed by God
records.note: "In Christ" is in the Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus but not in the early Alexandrian witnesses the critical text follows. Paul links the promise to Christ in 3:16.

records.change: "faith of Jesus Christ" becomes "faithfulness of the Messiah"
records.note: A translation choice: the ISV reads the genitive as Christ's faithfulness, not faith in him. The Greek is the same; "to them that believe" still states the believer's faith.

records.change: "heir of God through Christ" becomes "heir because of what God did"
records.note: The Textus Receptus reads "heir of God through Christ"; the critical text, with early Alexandrian witnesses, reads "heir through God". Christ's role in sonship is stated in 4:4-6.

records.change: Omits "in Christ Jesus"
records.note: The opening "For in Christ Jesus" is in the Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus but not in Vaticanus and other early witnesses. Galatians 5:6 has the same thought with "in Christ Jesus".

records.change: "the Lord Jesus" becomes "Jesus"
records.note: The Textus Receptus reads "the Lord Jesus"; the critical text, with early Alexandrian witnesses, reads "Jesus" alone. The title Lord is dropped here only.

records.change: Omits "by Jesus Christ" as the one through whom God created
records.note: "By Jesus Christ" is in the Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus but not in Sinaiticus, Vaticanus or other early witnesses; the ISV also follows the reading "administration" rather than "fellowship". Creation through Christ is still stated in John 1:3 and Colossians 1:16.

records.change: "fruit of the Spirit" becomes "fruit that the light produces"
records.note: The Textus Receptus reads "Spirit", likely from Galatians 5:22; the critical text, following early papyri and Alexandrian witnesses, reads "light", which fits 5:8. The fruit of the Spirit is still named in Galatians 5:22.

records.change: "fear of God" becomes "reverence for the Messiah"
records.note: The Textus Receptus reads "God"; the critical text, with early witnesses, reads "Christ". Either reading grounds mutual submission in reverence for God or Christ.

records.change: "the Lord" becomes "the Messiah"
records.note: The Textus Receptus reads "Lord"; the critical text, with early witnesses, reads "Christ". The one caring for the church is the same.

records.change: Omits closing "Amen"
records.note: The "Amen" is in the Textus Receptus and later manuscripts but not in early Alexandrian witnesses. The closing subscription in the KJV is not part of the verse.

records.change: Verses 16 and 17 in reverse order
records.note: The critical text, following early witnesses, puts "of love" before "of contention"; the Textus Receptus has the reverse order. Nothing is lost; the KJV's verse 16 is the ISV's verse 17.

records.change: "in heaven, in earth, under the earth" becomes "wherever they're residing"
records.note: A translation choice: the Greek names three realms in all texts, and the ISV's paraphrase generalises them. Christ's universal lordship is still stated.

records.change: Omits "by the same rule, let us mind the same thing"
records.note: These words are in the Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus but not in early papyri and Alexandrian witnesses. Like-mindedness is urged elsewhere, as in 2:2.

records.change: "through Christ" becomes "through him"
records.note: The Textus Receptus names Christ; the critical text, with early witnesses, reads "him who strengthens me". The context of the letter makes Christ the referent.

records.change: Omits "and the Lord Jesus Christ" from the greeting
records.note: The words are in the Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus but not in Vaticanus and other early witnesses. Paul's other greetings name Christ with the Father.

records.change: Omits "through his blood"
records.note: The phrase is in later manuscripts and the Textus Receptus but not in Sinaiticus, Vaticanus or most early witnesses, and may come from Ephesians 1:7. Redemption through Christ's blood is still stated in Ephesians 1:7 and Colossians 1:20.

records.change: "Christ Jesus" becomes "the Messiah"
records.note: The Textus Receptus reads "Christ Jesus"; the critical text, with early witnesses, reads "Christ" alone. The referent is unchanged.

records.change: "of God, and of the Father, and of Christ" becomes "Messiah, mystery of God"
records.note: The Textus Receptus has the longer reading; the critical text, following Papyrus 46 and Vaticanus, reads "of God, Christ", making Christ the mystery. The Father is dropped here.

records.change: "Christ forgave you" becomes "the Lord has forgiven you"
records.note: The Textus Receptus reads "Christ"; the critical text, with early witnesses, reads "Lord". The one who forgives is the same.

records.change: "peace of God" becomes "peace of the Messiah"
records.note: The Textus Receptus reads "God"; the critical text, with early witnesses, reads "Christ". Both readings are attested elsewhere, as in Philippians 4:7 and John 14:27.

records.change: "to the Lord" becomes "to God"
records.note: The Textus Receptus reads "Lord"; the critical text, with early witnesses, reads "God". The ISV's "thankfulness" for "grace" is a translation choice.

records.change: "fearing God" becomes "fearing the Lord"
records.note: The Textus Receptus reads "God"; the critical text, with early witnesses, reads "the Lord". Reverence toward God is the point in either reading.

records.change: "our Lord Jesus Christ" becomes "our Lord Jesus"
records.note: "Christ" is in the Textus Receptus but not in the early witnesses the critical text follows. Only the title is shortened.

records.change: "our Lord Jesus Christ" becomes "our Lord Jesus"
records.note: "Christ" is in the Textus Receptus but not in Sinaiticus, Vaticanus and other early witnesses. Only the title is shortened.

records.change: "our Lord Jesus Christ" becomes "our Lord Jesus"
records.note: "Christ" is in the Textus Receptus but not in the early witnesses the critical text follows. Only the title is shortened.

records.change: "our Lord Jesus Christ" becomes "our Lord Jesus"
records.note: "Christ" is in the Textus Receptus but not in Vaticanus and other early witnesses. Only the title is shortened.

records.change: First "Christ" dropped; ends "our God and Lord, Jesus"
records.note: The critical text lacks the first "Christ" found in the Textus Receptus. The ISV also reads the closing phrase as one person, "our God and Lord, Jesus", a translation choice that calls Christ God.

records.change: "day of Christ" becomes "Day of the Lord"
records.note: The Textus Receptus reads "Christ"; the critical text, with early witnesses, reads "Lord". Both refer to Christ's coming.

records.change: Omits "as God" before "sitteth in the temple"
records.note: "As God" is in the Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus but not in early Alexandrian witnesses. The claim to be God is still made at the end of the verse.

records.change: "from the beginning chosen you" becomes "chose you... first fruits"
records.note: The Greek manuscripts divide between "from the beginning" (Textus Receptus) and "as first fruits" (Vaticanus and others), which differ by one letter. The choosing to salvation is kept, but not that it was from the beginning.

records.change: "Lord Jesus Christ" becomes "the Messiah Jesus"
records.note: The Textus Receptus reads "Lord Jesus Christ"; the critical text, with early witnesses, reads "Christ Jesus". The title Lord is dropped here.

records.change: Omits "in Christ" from "I speak the truth"
records.note: "In Christ" is in the Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus but not in Sinaiticus and other early witnesses. Paul's oath of truthfulness is otherwise kept.

records.change: "God was manifest in the flesh" becomes "he was revealed"
records.note: Later manuscripts and the Textus Receptus read "God"; Sinaiticus and other early witnesses read "who", which the ISV renders "he". The ISV's poetic rendering also adds "our Lord in heaven reigning". Christ's deity is stated elsewhere, as in Titus 2:13.

records.change: Omits "in spirit" from the list
records.note: "In spirit" is in the Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus but not in the early witnesses the critical text follows. The other qualities are kept.

records.change: "the Lord Jesus Christ" becomes "the Messiah Jesus"
records.note: The Textus Receptus reads "Lord Jesus Christ"; the critical text, with early witnesses, reads "Christ Jesus". The title Lord is dropped here.

records.change: Omits "from such withdraw thyself"
records.note: The command is in the Byzantine text and Textus Receptus but not in Sinaiticus, Alexandrinus and other early witnesses; similar instruction appears in 2 Timothy 3:5.

records.change: Omits closing "Amen"; "with thee" becomes "with all of you"
records.note: The Textus Receptus has "with thee. Amen"; the critical text, with early witnesses, has the plural and no "Amen". The KJV's closing subscription is not part of the verse.

records.change: "before the Lord" becomes "before God"
records.note: Manuscripts divide between "Lord" (Textus Receptus and many others) and "God" (Sinaiticus and others). The charge is solemn in either reading.

records.change: "name of Christ" becomes "name of the Lord"
records.note: The Textus Receptus reads "Christ"; the critical text, with early witnesses, reads "Lord". The one named is the same.

records.change: "the Lord Jesus Christ" becomes "the Messiah Jesus"
records.note: The Textus Receptus reads "the Lord Jesus Christ"; the critical text, with early witnesses, reads "Christ Jesus". Christ as judge of the living and dead is kept.

records.change: "The Lord Jesus Christ" becomes "the Lord"
records.note: "Jesus Christ" is in the Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus but not in Sinaiticus and other early witnesses. The KJV's closing subscription is not part of the verse.

records.change: Omits "mercy"; "the Lord Jesus Christ" becomes "the Messiah, Jesus"
records.note: The Textus Receptus reads "grace, mercy, and peace" and "Lord Jesus Christ"; the critical text, with early witnesses, has "grace and peace" and "Christ Jesus". Christ is still called Saviour.

records.change: "Christ Jesus" becomes "the Messiah"
records.note: The Textus Receptus reads "Christ Jesus"; the critical text, with early witnesses, reads "Christ". The ISV's "ours" for "in you" also follows a variant.

records.change: Second "in the Lord" becomes "in the Messiah"
records.note: The Textus Receptus reads "Lord"; the critical text, with early witnesses, reads "Christ". The referent is the same.

records.change: Omits "by himself" and "our" before sins
records.note: The Textus Receptus reads "by himself" and "our sins"; Sinaiticus, Vaticanus and other early witnesses lack them. Christ's own sacrifice for sins is still stated in Hebrews 9:26 and 10:12.

records.change: "have I begotten thee" becomes "I have become your Father"
records.note: A translation choice: the Greek "begotten" is the same in all texts, and the ISV renders it by its sense. The word the KJV uses for the Son's begetting is lost here.

records.change: Omits "and didst set him over the works of thy hands"
records.note: The clause is in Sinaiticus and the Textus Receptus but not in Papyrus 46, Vaticanus and the Byzantine majority; it is part of the quoted Psalm 8:6. Dominion over all things is still stated in 2:8.

records.change: "Christ Jesus" becomes "Jesus"
records.note: The Textus Receptus reads "Christ Jesus"; the critical text, with early witnesses, reads "Jesus" alone. Only the title is shortened.

records.change: "have I begotten thee" becomes "I have become your Father"
records.note: A translation choice: the Greek "begotten" is the same in all texts, and the ISV renders it by its sense. The word the KJV uses for the Son's begetting is lost here.

records.change: Omits "after the order of Melchisedec"
records.note: The phrase is in the Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus but not in early witnesses such as Papyrus 46 and Sinaiticus; it may come from 7:17. The Melchizedek priesthood is still stated in 7:17.

records.change: Omits "O God" from the quotation
records.note: "O God" is in later manuscripts and the Textus Receptus but not in the early witnesses the critical text follows; it may come from 10:7. God is still addressed in 10:7.

records.change: Omits "saith the Lord"
records.note: The words are in the Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus but not in Papyrus 46 and other early witnesses. The quotation's divine source is plain from the second line.

records.change: Omits "in heaven"; "me in my bonds" becomes "the prisoners"
records.note: The Textus Receptus reads "my bonds" and "in heaven"; the critical text, with early witnesses, reads "the prisoners" and lacks "in heaven". The better, lasting possession is kept.

records.change: Omits closing "Amen"
records.note: The "Amen" is in the Textus Receptus and most manuscripts but not in Papyrus 46 and some early witnesses. The KJV's closing subscription is not part of the verse.

records.change: "the Lord hath promised" becomes "God has promised"
records.note: The Textus Receptus names "the Lord"; the critical text, with early witnesses, has no subject ("he promised"), which the ISV fills with "God". The promise is the same.

records.change: "God, even the Father" becomes "the Lord and Father"
records.note: The Textus Receptus reads "God"; the critical text, with early witnesses, reads "Lord". The one blessed is the same.

records.change: Omits "through the Spirit"
records.note: The phrase is in the Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus but not in the early witnesses the critical text follows. The Spirit's sanctifying work is still stated in 1:2.

records.change: Adds "in your salvation"
records.note: "Into salvation" is in Sinaiticus, Vaticanus and most early witnesses but not in the Textus Receptus. It presents salvation as something grown into.

records.change: "the Lord God" becomes "the Messiah as Lord"
records.note: The Textus Receptus reads "God"; the critical text, with early witnesses, reads "Christ", which applies Isaiah 8:13's words about the LORD to Christ. The ISV's "with meekness and fear" is not lost but at the start of 3:16.

records.change: Omits "for us"
records.note: "For us" is in the Byzantine text and Textus Receptus but not in Vaticanus and other early witnesses. Christ's suffering for others is still stated in 1 Peter 3:18.

records.change: Omits "on their part he is evil spoken of...glorified"
records.note: The closing clause is in the Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus but not in Papyrus 72, Sinaiticus or Vaticanus. The blessing on those reproached for Christ is kept.

records.change: Omits "Jesus" and the closing "Amen"
records.note: "Jesus" and "Amen" are in the Textus Receptus but not in the early witnesses the critical text follows. The benediction is otherwise kept.

records.change: Omits "for ever" from darkness reserved for them
records.note: "For ever" is in the Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus but not in early witnesses; it may come from Jude 13. Jude 13 still says the darkness is reserved for ever.

records.change: "the blood of Jesus Christ" becomes "the blood of Jesus"
records.note: "Christ" is in the Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus but not in Sinaiticus, Vaticanus and others. Cleansing by his blood is kept.

records.change: "love of God, because he laid down" becomes "the Messiah gave"
records.note: "Of God" is printed in italics in the KJV as a supplied word; the Greek reads "we have known love". The KJV's wording implies God laid down his life, which the ISV's "the Messiah" does not.

records.change: Omits "Christ is come in the flesh"; reads "acknowledge Jesus"
records.note: The Textus Receptus repeats the confession of 4:2; the critical text, following Sinaiticus, Alexandrinus and Vaticanus, reads only "confesses not Jesus". The incarnation is still confessed in 4:2.

records.change: "only begotten Son" becomes "unique Son"
records.note: A translation choice: the Greek "monogenes" is the same in all texts, and the ISV reads it as "one of a kind" rather than "only begotten". The Son's unique relation to the Father is kept, but not the idea of begetting.

records.change: Omits "the Father, the Word, and the Holy Ghost" in heaven
records.note: The Johannine Comma is in the Textus Receptus and a few late Greek manuscripts and Latin witnesses, but not in the Greek manuscripts before the late Middle Ages; the ISV follows the latter. The Trinity is still taught in passages such as Matthew 28:19.

records.change: Omits "in earth"; the three witnesses joined to 5:7
records.note: "In earth" belongs to the Johannine Comma, which the critical text omits with the Greek manuscript tradition; the ISV's 5:7 begins the sentence. The three earthly witnesses are kept.

records.change: Omits "that ye may believe on the name of the Son"
records.note: The Textus Receptus has the closing clause; the critical text, following Sinaiticus, Vaticanus and others, lacks it and has "to you who believe" earlier. Belief in the Son's name is still stated.

records.change: "begotten of God keepeth himself" becomes "the Son of God protects"
records.note: Manuscripts divide between "himself" (Textus Receptus, Sinaiticus) and "him" (Alexandrinus, Vaticanus); the ISV reads "him" and takes the begotten one as Christ. Either reading keeps the believer safe from the evil one.

records.change: Omits closing "Amen"
records.note: The "Amen" is in the Textus Receptus and later manuscripts but not in the early witnesses the critical text follows.

records.change: "the Lord Jesus Christ" becomes "Jesus the Messiah"
records.note: The Textus Receptus reads "the Lord Jesus Christ"; the critical text, with early witnesses, lacks "Lord". It also reads "with us" for "with you".

records.change: Omits closing "Amen"
records.note: The "Amen" is in the Textus Receptus and later manuscripts but not in the early witnesses the critical text follows.

records.change: "the only Lord God, and our Lord" becomes "our only Master and Lord"
records.note: The Textus Receptus has "God"; the critical text, with early papyri and Alexandrian witnesses, lacks it, so both titles fall to Jesus alone. God the Father is not named in the denial.

records.change: Omits "wise"; adds "through Jesus the Messiah, our Lord"
records.note: The critical text, following early witnesses, lacks "wise" and adds "through Jesus Christ our Lord" and "before all time"; the Textus Receptus has "only wise God". The ISV makes Christ the mediator of the doxology.

records.change: Omits "and of all things that he saw"
records.note: The phrase is in all Greek texts in some form, so this is a translation choice by the ISV. John's claim to have witnessed what he writes is weakened here.

records.change: "washed us from our sins in his blood" becomes "freed us"
records.note: The Textus Receptus reads "washed" (lousanti); the critical text, with early witnesses, reads "freed" (lusanti), which differ by one letter. Release from sin by Christ's blood is kept in both.

records.change: Omits "the beginning and the ending"; "Lord" becomes "Lord God"
records.note: Sinaiticus, Alexandrinus and most Greek manuscripts lack the title and read "Lord God"; the Textus Receptus follows a few late witnesses. The same title stands in Revelation 21:6 and 22:13.

records.change: "Jesus Christ" becomes "Jesus" twice
records.note: "Christ" is in the Textus Receptus in both places but not in the early witnesses the critical text follows. Only the title is shortened.

records.change: Omits "I am Alpha and Omega, the first and the last"
records.note: The words are in the Textus Receptus but not in the Greek manuscripts the critical text follows; "which are in Asia" is also absent. Christ still calls himself the first and the last in 1:17 and Alpha and Omega in 22:13.

records.change: Omits "Amen" after "alive for evermore"
records.note: The "Amen" is in the Textus Receptus but not in the early witnesses the critical text follows. Christ's living for ever is kept.

records.change: Omits "four and twenty" and "him that liveth for ever and ever"
records.note: The words are in the Textus Receptus but not in the Greek manuscripts the critical text follows. The elders' worship is kept, but its object is not named.

records.change: "an angel" becomes "an eagle"
records.note: The Textus Receptus reads "angel"; the critical text, following nearly all Greek manuscripts, reads "eagle". The woe pronounced is the same.

records.change: "God of the earth" becomes "Lord of the earth"
records.note: The Textus Receptus reads "God"; the critical text, with the majority of Greek manuscripts, reads "Lord". The one they stand before is the same.

records.change: Omits "and art to come"
records.note: The phrase is lacking in nearly all Greek manuscripts, including the Byzantine majority; the Textus Receptus has it from a few late witnesses. Without it the hymn presents God's coming as now fulfilled in his reign; the threefold title stands in 1:4, 1:8 and 4:8.

records.change: "Jesus Christ" becomes "Jesus"
records.note: "Christ" is in the Textus Receptus but not in the Greek manuscripts the critical text follows. Only the title is shortened.

records.change: Omits "before the throne of God"
records.note: The phrase is in the Textus Receptus but not in the Greek manuscripts the critical text follows. The blamelessness of the 144,000 is kept.

records.change: Omits "O Lord"; "shalt be" becomes "the Holy One"
records.note: The Textus Receptus reads "O Lord" and "shalt be" (a reading from Beza's edition); the Greek manuscripts read "the Holy One". God's holiness replaces his future existence in this verse.

records.change: Omits "of heaven" after "temple"
records.note: "Of heaven" is in the Textus Receptus but not in the early witnesses the critical text follows. The voice from the throne is kept.

records.change: "unto the Lord our God" becomes "our God"; omits "honour"
records.note: The Textus Receptus has "honour" and "the Lord"; the critical text, with the early witnesses, lacks both. The praise to God is kept.

records.change: "supper of the great God" becomes "great supper of God"
records.note: The Textus Receptus reads "the supper of the great God"; the critical text, with early witnesses, reads "the great supper of God". The title "great God" is lost here.

records.change: "stand before God" becomes "standing in front of the throne"
records.note: The Textus Receptus reads "God"; the critical text, with the Greek manuscripts, reads "the throne". The judgment is the same.

records.change: Adds "the lake of fire" after "second death"
records.note: The critical text, with early witnesses, has "the second death, the lake of fire"; the Textus Receptus lacks the last words. The addition restates what the verse already says.

records.change: "out of heaven" becomes "from the throne"
records.note: The Textus Receptus reads "heaven"; the critical text, with early witnesses, reads "the throne". The message of God dwelling with people is kept.

records.change: "God shall wipe away" becomes "He will wipe"
records.note: "God" is in the Textus Receptus but not in the early witnesses the critical text follows. The subject is plain from 21:3.

records.change: Omits "of them which are saved" and "and honour"
records.note: The words are in the Textus Receptus but not in the Greek manuscripts the critical text follows. Without them the verse speaks of the nations in general.

records.change: "do his commandments" becomes "wash their robes"
records.note: The Textus Receptus and the Byzantine majority read "do his commandments"; Sinaiticus and Alexandrinus read "wash their robes", which the ISV follows. The two readings give different grounds for the right to the tree of life.

records.change: "book of life" becomes "tree of life"
records.note: Almost all Greek manuscripts read "tree"; "book" entered the Textus Receptus through Erasmus, whose Greek copy lacked these verses and was supplied from the Latin Vulgate. The book of life is still named in 3:5, 20:15 and 21:27.

records.change: "our Lord Jesus Christ" becomes "the Lord Jesus"; "all the saints"
records.note: "Our" and "Christ" are in the Textus Receptus but not in Alexandrinus; the manuscripts also divide between "you all" and "all the saints". The benediction is otherwise kept.
